articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cartel del Noreste Facilitators and Horse Racing Enterprise
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned four individuals and eleven entities for their involvement in the Cartel del Noreste (CDN) and its expansive criminal network. This action targets the cartel's horse racing enterprise and other facilitators.

Among the designated individuals is Gamaliel Garza Elias, identified with a birthdate of July 10, 1997, and a place of birth in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, Mexico. The entities added to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List include Club La Molienda, Cuadra San DibanH, Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V., Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V., and Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V., all linked to the CDN's operations.

This action underscores OFAC's ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial networks of transnational criminal organizations, particularly those involved in illicit drug trafficking and other criminal activities that pose a threat to U.S. national security.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License for Diesel Fuel Imports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Russia-related General License 135, authorizing certain transactions related to the sale, delivery, offloading, and importation of diesel fuel of Russian Federation origin. This license is effective through April 7, 2027.

This action follows an announcement by the U.S. President regarding a deal with Russia to release 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to global markets, with additional amounts expected in the coming months, aiming to ease rising diesel prices worldwide.

However, the General License does not authorize any debit to an account on the books of a U.S. financial institution of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, the National Wealth Fund of the Russian Federation, or the Ministry of Finance. It also does not affect Russia-related sanctions imposed by other members of the Price Cap Coalition, such as the UK and EU.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities, Issues New Iran-Related and Amended Russia-Related General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting Iran's shadow fleet network. Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran-related General License EE, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving Samudra Marine Services Private Limited.

Additionally, OFAC issued Russia-related General License 13S, which authorizes certain administrative transactions prohibited by Directive 4 under Executive Order 14024. This move further intensifies sanctions against Iran's economy, building on previous actions against its aviation, automotive, and rail sectors.

The designations and general licenses reflect OFAC's ongoing strategy to disrupt Iran's ability to fund its missile and cyber programs and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) by isolating key sectors of its economy and targeting foreign suppliers.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes 125 Entities, Updates Sanctions Lists, and Issues Iran-Related Alert
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a significant round of sanctions modernization, removing 125 individuals and entities from its sanctions lists and updating 22 additional entries. These removals include deceased individuals, defunct companies, and entries lacking sufficient identifying information.

In conjunction with these updates, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert, 'Notice to Foreign Financial Institutions Conducting Business with Iran,' warning that foreign financial institutions transacting with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification.

OFAC also published an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 156), removing previous language that indicated OFAC would generally contact a foreign financial institution before making a finding of sanctionable activity. This emphasizes the heightened risk for foreign financial institutions involved in Iran-related transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities in Counter Terrorism Action
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Counter Terrorism Designations. This action targets individuals and entities involved in supporting terrorist organizations.

While specific details of the newly designated parties were not immediately released in the summary, these actions are part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial networks of global terrorist groups.
This follows previous actions targeting Hamas's financial network and other groups, demonstrating a continued focus on combating terrorism financing through sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Automotive and Rail Sectors, Updates Sanctions Lists
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and updates, specifically targeting the automotive and rail sectors of the Iranian economy. This action includes a determination under Executive Order 13902, identifying these sectors as subject to sanctions.

Simultaneously, OFAC designated Iranian automotive and rail companies, foreign automotive suppliers, manufacturing and metals-sector companies, and participants in a steel and oil export network. This expands the scope of 'Operation Economic Outcast' to further isolate Iran's industrial base.

Additionally, OFAC published an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question, providing further guidance on the expanded sanctions. This move aims to cut off funding to the Iranian government and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Sanctions from Entities and Individuals Under Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Programs
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced the removal of several entities and individuals from its sanctions lists under the Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya programs. This action also included new Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations.

Among those delisted were Patraca S.A., an entity previously sanctioned under counter-narcotics programs, the cargo ship Maraya (also referred to as Med Patron), formerly designated under Libya sanctions, and Tatyana Protopovich, who was previously sanctioned in connection with Belarus.
These removals reflect ongoing administrative processes to update and refine sanctions lists, potentially allowing the delisted parties to re-engage with the U.S. financial system.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Sanctions on Iran-Related, Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, and Non-Proliferation Networks
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a broad range of new designations targeting Iran-related, Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, and Non-Proliferation networks. This action is part of an intensified campaign to disrupt illicit activities globally.

The Iran-related designations specifically target military procurement networks supporting Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL), which oversees the country's ballistic missile and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) programs.

Additionally, OFAC designated individuals and entities linked to the Sinaloa Cartel's Los Mayos faction and associated corruption networks, further demonstrating a comprehensive approach to combating transnational threats.

articles.headline: Russian Diesel Imports Authorized by OFAC to Stabilize Global Prices
body: The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued General License 135, temporarily authorizing transactions involving Russian-origin diesel fuel until April 7, 2027. This move aims to address rising global diesel prices and follows an agreement with Russia to release significant quantities of diesel to international markets.

The authorization is expected to bring over 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, with further shipments planned to potentially reach 3 million tons. This initiative is a direct response to global energy market instability and recent U.S. legislation targeting Russia's energy sector.

Despite the potential relief for global energy markets, concerns remain regarding Russia's ability to meet the proposed volumes, especially given reports of pressure on its own fuel industry and claims of damage to its refining capacity.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11,662,930 Over Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to pay $11,662,930 to settle its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

The violations involved sanctions programs targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism. OFAC determined that the apparent violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed by the bank.

The settlement amount reflects OFAC's determination that the violations were not voluntarily disclosed and that the bank failed to appropriately prioritize alerts for customers matching blocked persons, promptly update watchlists, and mishandled accounts due to human error.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Settles with OFAC for $175,015 for Sanctions Violations
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a California-based freight forwarding firm, has agreed to pay $175,015 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

The violations occurred between September 2023 and February 2024, when Pegasus facilitated the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company and failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months.

OFAC determined that Pegasus's conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed. The settlement amount reflects a 15 percent reduction from the base penalty, acknowledging the company's extensive remedial measures and enhanced reporting commitments.

articles.headline: Individual Settles with OFAC for $1,427,230 for Iran Sanctions Violations
body: An individual has agreed to pay $1,427,230 to settle potential civil liability for apparent violations of Iran sanctions. The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) determined that the apparent violations were egregious and not voluntarily self-disclosed.
This enforcement action is part of OFAC's aggressive campaign to hold accountable U.S. and foreign persons who violate Iran sanctions, particularly under 'Operation Economic Outcast.'
The investigation and resolution of this matter were conducted in cooperation with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Los Angeles Field Office, Orange County Resident Agency.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

body: An in-depth look at the key polling, races and issues ahead of an election that will define Trump’s final two years as president.

articles.headline: Inside Katie Zacharia's very brief White House briefing
body: The BBC's Sarah Smith was in the room and describes Zacharia's performance and the moment she broke news about Kimberly Guilfoyle being asked to resign.

articles.headline: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
body: Student protesters in France have told the BBC's James Waterhouse that they will continue to take action until change has been made. The protests have now entered their fourth week.

articles.headline: BBC's Orla Guerin travels with Yemen's southern national security forces through desert battlefield
body: Orla Guerin travelled through Yemen, with forces loyal to its internationally recognised government, to a remote desert battlefield where Houthi rebels were dislodged just days ago.
